children: Egyptian developer M squared has started construction of Phase 2 of its 1,546-unit Masyaf Ras Alhekma development on Egypt's North Coast, with overall construction reaching approximately 41 percent, the company said on Wednesday.

Construction is under way across the entirety of Phase 1, comprising 347 units scheduled for delivery by the end of 2027, it said in a press statement. M squared has delivered 160 units at the development to date.
The statement said Redcon Construction has joined the project as a major construction partner, with work under way on the Lagoon Buildings and construction initiated on all Phase 1 lagoons.
Around 700 million Egyptian pounds ($14 million) worth of construction and development works were carried out across Masyaf during 2026, the statement noted.
The company is also preparing to start a shoreline protection and enhancement project in October 2026 after securing approvals from the relevant authorities.

International water and coastal engineering specialist from Denmark DHI designed the scheme, which will address erosion and flooding control, protect the sandy beach and improve swimmer safety, the statement said.

M squared has also expanded Masyaf's water infrastructure, increasing the capacity of its desalination plant to 1,000 cubic metres per day (m3/day) and adding water wells to support the development's growth.

The project's hospitality and commercial offering has expanded alongside construction. The number of operating F&B, retail, wellness and lifestyle outlets and services increased to 35 in 2026 from 17 in 2025.

Marmarica Boutique Cabanas is operating with 42 keys in 2026, comprising pool and seafront cabanas, rooms and suites. M squared has appointed Impact Hospitality Group, the organisation behind Casa Cook, to operate the property.
The developer has also partnered with Fairmont Nile City on the operation of Saigon by the Sea and Olive Tree at Masyaf.
Sales have reached 70 percent of the project's total units, the statement noted.
(Writing by Marwa Abo Almajd; Editing by Anoop Menon)
